defects.trigger: applyRate(cents, basisPoints) called with basisPoints > 10000, e.g. applyRate(100, 10001) or applyRate(1000, 15000)
defects.reason: applyRate only validates that basisPoints is a non-negative safe integer (`!Number.isSafeInteger(basisPoints) || basisPoints < 0`); there is no upper bound check. Acceptance condition 5 requires a TypeError for any rate above 100% (i.e. basisPoints > 10000), so rates above 100% are silently accepted and applied.
defects.impact: Contract violation of the authoritative acceptance condition 5: out-of-range rates are computed instead of rejected, so callers passing a percentage-by-mistake (10001, 15000, 1000000) get a silently inflated/deflated result. The repository gate (tools/accept.mjs) has no assertion for this bound, so a green gate does not cover it.
defects.repro: node --input-type=module -e "import {applyRate} from './src/invoice.mjs'; console.log(applyRate(100,10001), applyRate(1000,15000))" -> prints '100 1500' instead of throwing TypeError. See review-evidence/probe.log (basisPoints boundary probe: 10000=>1000, 10001=>1000, 10002=>1000, 15000=>1500, 1000000=>100000).

blockers: Acceptance condition 5 is unmet (see defect): applyRate accepts basisPoints > 10000 instead of throwing a TypeError.

interpretations.text: basisPoints > 10000 (rate above 100%) must throw a TypeError. The bound is on the basisPoints argument, so 10000 itself is valid (100%) and only values strictly greater than 10000 must throw. tools/accept.mjs contains no assertion for this bound, so the passing gate alone cannot establish condition 5 — it was checked directly against the candidate source.

handoff.conclusion: Conditions 1-4 are satisfied: rounding is half-away-from-zero for both signs, allocate ranks fractional remainders with ties to the earlier line and sums exactly, tools/accept.mjs and test/ are byte-identical to baseline, and the candidate commit 455c42a is committed with a green acceptance command (427 assertions) and unit suite (3/3). Condition 5 is NOT satisfied: applyRate has no upper bound on basisPoints, so applyRate(100, 10001) returns 100 and applyRate(1000, 15000) returns 1500 instead of throwing a TypeError. Verdict CHANGES_REQUESTED.
handoff.next: Add an upper-bound guard in applyRate that throws TypeError when basisPoints > 10000 (keeping 10000 itself valid and leaving tools/accept.mjs and test/ untouched), then commit and re-run the acceptance command.
